difficulty_reason: The author constructs a family of double-plane K3 surfaces, controls geometric Picard number one through reductions and preserves a genus-one curve with a non-torsion rational point, then proves the family dominates the degree-two K3 moduli space. Density refers to the surface locus in moduli; each individual surface is asserted to have infinitely many Q-rational points. The universal degree-12 extension bound and supporting dominance lemma are context, not additional counts.
